title: Fallback decision-graph corruption postmortem and remediation
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a capacity churn event on 2026-02-17 we observed multiple customer requests being routed to incompatible model variants and, in some regions, entering a cross-region reroute loop. The immediate effect was increased latencies (p95 spike to >6s) and elevated error rates for specific tenant traffic. This ticket contains the incident summary, root cause analysis, and concrete action items for preventing recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-17T02:12:00Z - First anomaly: spike in error rate for subset of requests routed through smart-routing cluster eu-west-1.
2026-02-17T02:13:30Z - Autoscaler for dedicated pools began rapid scale-down due to misinterpreted liveness signals (capacity churn).
2026-02-17T02:14:10Z - New routing policy bundle (policy v2026-02-17-0210) was published as part of a routine config push.
2026-02-17T02:15:20Z - Fallback decision-graph entries in Redis showed corrupted adjacency lists (missing variant weights).
2026-02-17T02:16:45Z - Smart routing decision loop detected: requests bounced between eu-west-1 and us-east-1 due to incompatible variant checks and TTL refresh race.

2026-02-17T02:20:00Z - On-call engineer applied emergency mitigation: disable new policy bundle and force sticky routing to last-known-good variant; errors dropped and latencies returned to baseline by 02:34.
2026-02-17T03:10:00Z - Incident declared resolved; post-incident triage scheduled.
scope: Requests processed by smart-routing service between 02:12 and 02:34 UTC on 2026-02-17. Affected tenants: ~4% of active traffic (mix of hosted and dedicated), primarily using pinned model groups that had recent variant updates.
impact_summary: High-severity customer impact: transient request failures (5xx) and p95 latency regression. Some customers saw model mismatch errors where the runtime returned responses from a model variant that didn't support the requested schema (function-calling calls failed). Billing was not materially affected but customer SLAs were at risk.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate policy bundle publish while making a concurrent capacity change to a dedicated pool (scale down followed by scale up within <60s).
2) Ensure the policy contains a variant replacement for a model family with different schema capabilities (e.g., function-calling enabled vs disabled).
3) Run high volume of short requests to surface routing decision race and cached adjacency read/write collisions.

Observed: decision-graph entries stored in Redis can be partially written if a config write is interleaved with a cache rebuild task, leading to malformed variant metadata that causes incorrect fallback decisions.
root_cause: A race condition between the policy-publish path and the decision-graph cache rebuild produced partially-applied adjacency data in Redis. The cache rebuild writes multiple keys without atomicity; in rare interleavings a consumer read obtains a malformed adjacency list (missing variant weight/compatibility flags). The fallback evaluator assumed adjacency entries were present and defaulted to the first listed variant, which could be incompatible. Additionally, TTL refresh logic for sticky routing erroneously re-enqueued stale route entries causing cross-region reroutes when the preferred pool became transiently unavailable.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back the policy bundle and forced a sticky-routing override to last-known-good model variants. Added a short-term Redis read validation that rejects adjacency lists missing required fields and falls back to a safe default (local fail-open) to prevent loops while a long-term fix is developed.
long_term_fix: 1) Change decision-graph updates to use atomic multi-key writes via Redis Lua script or single transaction to guarantee full adjacency consistency (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-05).
2) Add strict schema validation on reads with metrics and alerts when inconsistency detected (owner: Carlos Rivera, due: 2026-03-12).
3) Replace TTL-based sticky refresh with explicit lease-based locks to avoid re-enqueuing stale routes (owner: Lars Jensen, due: 2026-03-20).
4) Add canary rollout checks for policy bundles: validate decision-graph integrity in a canary region and hold global publish on failed checks (owner: Sita Patel, due: 2026-03-18).
5) Create a chaos test that simulates concurrent policy publish + autoscaler churn to catch regressions (owner: Reliability Team, due: 2026-04-01).
action_items: A-1: Implement atomic decision-graph write path (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/smart-routing/pull/2689). Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-05.
A-2: Implement read-side validation and a metric that increments on invalid adjacency reads. Owner: Carlos Rivera. Due: 2026-03-12.
A-3: Replace TTL sticky-refresh with lease-based approach; rollout behind feature flag. Owner: Lars Jensen. Due: 2026-03-20.
A-4: Add pre-publish canary verification job and gating in deployment pipeline. Owner: Sita Patel. Due: 2026-03-18.
A-5: Run post-fix incident drill with oncall and SRE to validate rollback and mitigation playbooks. Owner: Maya Chen. Due: 2026-03-28.
A-6: Add a dashboard panel for routing loop detection (Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/boards/routing-loop). Owner: Reliability Team. Due: 2026-03-08.
A-7: Update runbook to include steps for quickly forcing sticky routing and disabling policy bundles. Owner: Support Docs. Due: 2026-03-04.
acceptance_criteria: Atomic write implementation merged and deployed to canary region.
Read-side validation metric created and no invalid reads observed in 7 days post-deploy.
TTL->lease migration feature-flagged and shown to prevent re-enqueue during synthetic churn test.
Canary verification job blocks global publish when integrity checks fail (test coverage added).
follow_up_notes: We observed that only a small subset of policy bundles exercised adjacency updates frequently; those are highest-risk and will get dedicated unit tests.
SRE will add a synthetic canary that publishes a malformed bundle weekly to ensure detection paths remain functional.
Plan to present findings in next Platform Reliability review and prioritize funding for reliability labs that can run concurrent config+autoscale experiments.
